prompt:
The batch cannot leave the workshop until the three samples are sounded and photographed together, so all of them lie on the bench with a clip tuner at each head.

Three recorders of one model lie side by side, labelled A, B and C on their feet, every finger hole numbered from the mouthpiece end, hole 1 nearest the mouth. Black tape covers some holes on each: A over holes 1, 2 and 3; B over holes 1, 2, 3, 5 and 6; C over holes 1 and 2. Each has been blown steadily and its tuner left holding the note it gave. The workshop table pinned at the back of the bench says: with hole 3 the first left open the instrument sounds E5, with hole 4 the first left open it sounds D5, with hole 5 the first left open it sounds C5.

What each of the three tuners now displays is the whole of the check and the table does not display it.
easy_question: Does this picture show several recorders lying side by side with a small electronic tuner at the head of each? Answer yes or no only.

steps.ask: Read the note on the tuner display in front of the recorder labelled A and the note on the tuner display in front of the recorder labelled B. Answer with one of: the two displays show the same note as each other; the two displays show different notes from each other.
Read the note on the tuner display in front of the recorder labelled C. Answer with one of: the display shows D5; the display shows E5; the display shows C5.
